facts.statement: The genus Australotadorna was described by Worthy in 2009.
Australotadorna lived during the Late Oligocene epoch.
Australotadorna alecwilsoni is an extinct bird belonging to the shelduck subfamily of the duck family.
facts.quote: Australotadorna alecwilsoni is an extinct genus and species of bird, in the shelduck subfamily of the duck family

facts.statement: This species lived in central Australia during the Late Oligocene.
facts.quote: from the Late Oligocene of central Australia

facts.statement: The species name alecwilsoni honors Alec Wilson, a pastoral lease holder who supported fossil research on his property.
facts.quote: The specific epithet honours Alec Wilson, pastoral lease holder of Frome Downs Station, who supported palaeontological access to, and investigation of, fossil sites on his property

facts.statement: The type locality for Australotadorna is Lake Pinpa in the Lake Eyre Basin of north-eastern South Australia.
facts.quote: The type locality is Lake Pinpa in the Lake Eyre Basin of north-eastern South Australia

facts.statement: Australotadorna is classified within the tribe Tadornini.
Australotadorna belongs to the family Anatidae.
The fossil record for Australotadorna spans from 27.3 to 23.04 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Chattian to Chattian (27.3 to 23.04 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Australotadorna is a member of the class Aves.
